paper.title: UFO2: The Desktop AgentOS
paper.central_claim: A deeply OS-integrated multi-agent AgentOS for Windows (HostAgent + application-specialised AppAgents, UIA+vision hybrid control detection, unified GUI-API Puppeteer, retrieval-based knowledge integration, speculative multi-action execution, PiP isolation) outperforms prior CUAs including Operator: even with GPT-4o it reaches 27.9% on WAA and 28.6% on OSWorld-W (vs Operator 20.8/14.3) and cuts steps.

evidence.quote: most existing CUAs remain conceptual prototypes, hindered by shallow OS integration, fragile screenshot-based interaction, and disruptive execution
They ignore rich system interfaces such as accessibility APIs, application process state, and native inter-process communication mechanisms
HostAgent decomposes it into a series of subtasks, each mapped to the application best suited to fulfill it.
The global execution plan is serialized into a finite state machine (FSM)
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit FSM controller with CONTINUE/ASSIGN/PENDING/FINISH/FAIL states.

evidence.quote: If a semantically equivalent API is available, Puppeteer prefers it over GUI automation for reliability and atomicity.
If an API fails or is unavailable ( e.g. , missing bindings or runtime permission errors), the system gracefully falls back to GUI-based control
Visual detections with Intersection-over-Union (IoU) greater than 10% against any UIA-derived control are discarded.
evidence.support_explanation: Fusion rule: UIA controls win; remaining visual detections become pseudo-UIA objects.

evidence.quote: Periodically, these logs are mined offline by a summarization module that distills successful trajectories into reusable Example records.
evidence.support_explanation: Experience persistence: success logs -> Example DB.

evidence.quote: (2) Runtime Validation: For each action, the system consults the Windows UIA API to verify the action’s preconditions
evidence.support_explanation: Speculative batch validated by OS-level checks, not by a model.

evidence.quote: Windows Agent Arena (WAA) ( 49 ) : Consists of 154 live automation tasks across 15 commonly used Windows applications
OSWorld-W ( 50 ) : A targeted subset of the OSWorld benchmark specifically tailored for Windows, comprising 49 live tasks
Reported baseline scores in OSWorld differ slightly from prior results focused on Ubuntu due to corrections in verification scripts and alignment with Windows-specific tasks (OSWorld-W).
each agent is restricted to a maximum of 30 execution steps per task
API integrations were selectively implemented for three office applications within OSWorld-W as illustrative examples; no APIs were introduced for the WAA tasks.
Operator | computer-use | 20.8% | 14.3%
We create 34 help documents tailored to benchmark tasks, each containing precise step-by-step instructions
evidence.support_explanation: Test-task-specific help documents authored by the team.

evidence.quote: For subsequent tasks, UFO 2 dynamically retrieves up to three relevant past execution logs to guide task planning and execution.
evidence.support_explanation: Self-experience retrieved for later benchmark tasks; source tasks vs test tasks unspecified.

evidence.quote: summarizes successful execution trajectories—validated by our Task Evaluator and archives them into a retrievable knowledge database
evidence.support_explanation: Success gate is the authors LLM Task Evaluator.

evidence.quote: includes an automated task evaluation engine based on LLM-as-a-judge
evidence.support_explanation: LLM judge, no agreement with scripts reported.
UIA-only OSWorld-W is 22.4 here but 16.3 as UFO2-base in Table 1.
Hybrid on OSWorld-W equals UIA-only SR (22.4) with GPT-4o although CRR>0.
GUI+API 22.4 (=11/49); ablation baseline differs from Table 3 UIA row definition.
'None' knowledge row OSWorld-W 22.4 equals GUI+API, not 16.3.

evidence.quote: We calculate ACS on the subset of tasks that both configurations successfully complete, ensuring a fair comparison.
evidence.support_explanation: ACS conditioned on jointly solved tasks (survivorship).
Subset sizes 30 and 10 tasks for step comparison.

evidence.quote: more than 62% of failures were attributed to Control Detection Failures
evidence.support_explanation: Error analysis on WAA for UFO2-base.

evidence.quote: Across all configurations, the LLM inference phase dominates total latency, averaging around 10 seconds per inference.
the fully integrated UFO 2 incurs only an additional 1 second per step for its hybrid control detection pipeline
Figure 23 shows that UFO 2 + Operator achieves higher success rates than running Operator alone, particularly on WAA (26.0% vs. 20.8%).
whenever an AppAgent identifies an action matching predefined risk criteria, it transitions into a dedicated PENDING state, pausing execution and actively prompting the user for confirmation
evidence.support_explanation: Safeguard: risky actions gated by user confirmation (no evaluation).

evidence.quote: Even when paired with general-purpose models like GPT-4o, UFO 2 outperforms dedicated CUAs by over 10%
Each task runs independently, and verification strictly follows the original scripts provided by each benchmark.
We find that even minimal wrappers ( e.g. , for OpenAI Operator ( 12 ) ) lead to tangible performance gains
a method for inducing commonly reused routines, i.e. , workflows , and selectively providing workflows to the agent to guide subsequent generations
evidence.support_explanation: Pinned neighbour for experience-derived guidance injection.

evidence.quote: We evaluate UFO 2 using two established Windows-centric automation benchmarks

signatures.object: Agent architecture and action interface on Windows: HostAgent (FSM, blackboard) delegating subtasks to per-application AppAgents whose Puppeteer chooses between registered native APIs and GUI actions.
signatures.information: Screenshots, UIA control metadata, SoM-annotated controls, OS process info; API registry; private and shared blackboard memory.
signatures.operation: Task decomposition into dependency-ordered subtasks; ReAct loop per AppAgent; API-first with GUI fallback; PENDING state for risky actions.
signatures.output: GUI event or API call per step.
signatures.conditions: App APIs exist (COM for Office) — 12 hand-written APIs for Word/Excel/PowerPoint; UIA available or visual fallback.
signatures.feedback: UIA state checks; execution result/error from API; user confirmation for risky steps.
signatures.selection_rule: Prefer semantically equivalent API; fallback on failure.
signatures.persistence: Session memory and blackboard within a session.
signatures.failure_boundary: Apps without APIs or UIA support (LibreOffice), plan errors on OSWorld-W.

signatures.object: Hybrid control detection: UIA controls plus OmniParser-v2 detections merged by IoU deduplication.
signatures.information: UIA tree + screenshot parsed by YOLOv8/Florence-2.
signatures.operation: Drop visual boxes with IoU>10% against UIA; wrap the rest as pseudo-UIA controls; SoM annotate.
signatures.output: Unified control list for the agent.
signatures.claimed_effect: Control Recovery Ratio 9.9% (WAA), up to 25% (OSWorld-W, o1).
signatures.failure_boundary: Vision-only worse than UIA on OSWorld-W (14.3 vs 22.4).

signatures.object: Knowledge substrate: help-document index and Example DB of summarised successful trajectories, retrieved into prompts.
signatures.information: 34 authored help docs tailored to benchmark tasks; past execution logs validated by an LLM Task Evaluator; retrieval top-1 doc, top-3 logs.
signatures.operation: Offline summarisation of success logs; embedding retrieval at run time.
signatures.claimed_effect: Plan Recovery Ratio up to 17.7%; WAA SR 23.4 -> 26.6.
signatures.failure_boundary: Benefit varies by model (o1 self-experience WAA 25.3 -> 20.8).

signatures.information: One LLM call predicts k actions; UIA validates each before execution.
signatures.operation: Batch predict, validate, execute, early-exit and replan.
signatures.selection_rule: First failed validation halts the batch
signatures.failure_boundary: ACS measured on jointly solved tasks only (10 tasks on OSWorld-W).

gap.author_gap: CUAs rely on screenshots and simulated input, ignoring accessibility/APIs and process state, and lock the user out of the desktop.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible and partially measured: 62% of WAA failures of the UIA-only base are control-detection failures and OSWorld-W errors are plan-heavy (author error analysis). The comparison with baselines is, however, a system-vs-system one with unequal access to APIs and authored knowledge.
lineage: UFO v1 (same group), NAVI/WAA, OmniAgent/OmniParser, Agent S, OpenAI Operator, Claude Computer Use - baselines in Table 1
gap.lineage_note: The pinned references.json contains no Windows desktop CUA; WAA/OSWorld numbers of baselines come from the paper and cited works; later work (UI-TARS-2, MAI-UI) is current_relevance only.
gap.closest_adjacent: UFO v1 (UIA + vision) and Agent S (hierarchy plus experience retrieval).
gap.residue: Latency (10 s/step LLM), UIA gaps in third-party apps, human-level gap.
gap.stakes: Practical desktop automation with non-disruptive execution.
gap.method_response: Make OS interfaces first-class: UIA+vision, APIs, FSM orchestration, retrieval knowledge, PiP.
gap.remaining_gap: Which components cause the gain once baselines get the same APIs and documents; test-task leakage in knowledge.

claims.text: UFO 2 outperforms Operator and other CUAs: WAA 27.9 vs 20.8; OSWorld-W 28.6 vs 14.3 (GPT-4o), 30.5/32.7 with o1.
claims.setting: WAA 154 tasks, OSWorld-W 49 tasks, 30 steps, benchmark scripts
claims.baseline_control: Five CUAs; baselines GPT-4o except Operator; UFO2 full includes 12 handwritten Office APIs (OSWorld-W), 34 task-tailored help docs and experience DB
claims.selection_vs_test: Knowledge and APIs authored for/derived from the evaluation tasks
claims.counterevidence: UFO2-base (no APIs, no docs) beats Operator by 2.6 (WAA) and 2.0 (OSWorld-W, one task); ablation baselines are inconsistent across tables.
claims.allowed_conclusion: UFO2 (authors configuration) scores higher than listed baselines on these two Windows benchmarks; the part attributable to OS integration as opposed to test-tailored resources is not separated.

claims.text: GUI+API raises success and reduces steps; hybrid detection recovers failures; knowledge integration reduces plan errors; speculation cuts steps by up to 51.5%.
claims.setting: OSWorld-W 49 tasks (APIs for 27 Office tasks) and WAA
claims.result_denominator: 49 and 154 tasks; ACS on subsets of 10-34 jointly solved tasks
claims.counterevidence: OSWorld-W UIA-only baselines are 22.4 (Tables 3, 6, 7) and 16.3 (Tables 1, 5); hybrid equals UIA SR for GPT-4o on OSWorld-W; o1 self-experience lowers WAA SR (25.3 -> 20.8).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Directionally plausible component benefits; magnitudes are not reliable.

claims.text: PiP isolation lets users work concurrently.
claims.counterevidence: No evaluation of PiP or safeguard.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On WAA (154) and OSWorld-W (49) with a 30-step cap, the full UFO 2 configuration scores 27.9/28.6 (GPT-4o) vs 20.8/14.3 for Operator in single runs, and the UIA-only base already exceeds Operator on WAA by 2.6 points; the contribution of OS integration versus test-tailored APIs/documents/experience, and the individual component magnitudes, are not established.
unresolved: Experience DB overlap with test tasks
assessment.retention: Experience path: before (no DB) -> candidate Example records from logged runs -> selection (only trajectories validated by the Task Evaluator as success) -> persisted in application-specific example DB -> retrieved (top 3) for subsequent tasks -> gain WAA 23.4 -> 26.6 (GPT-4o) but -4.5 for o1 on WAA; the retained gain depends on whether source runs include evaluation tasks, which is unreported.

G.reason: Gap is concrete in systems terms (no access to accessibility/API state; disruptive control), tied to a measured failure breakdown (62% control detection failures on WAA base) and baseline systems; not 4 because the nearest neighbour UFO v1 and Agent S are not pinned/compared in mechanism and the 7-contribution scope spreads the gap thin.

M.reason: Each module has a stated mechanism and a checkable signal (UIA preconditions for speculative batches, API-first routing, IoU fusion, FSM states), and the error analysis motivates the hybrid/knowledge additions; the problem-fit of the bundled design (which component addresses which residue) is partly tested by ablations but hampered by inconsistent baselines.

X.reason: Architecture, state machines, fusion rule, API registry, retrieval flow and speculation loop are reconstructable with parameters like IoU 10% and caps (30 steps, top-1 doc, top-3 logs); deductions for no prompts, garbled Algorithm 1, unspecified action-selection policy between API and GUI, and unspecified composition of the Table 1 "full" configuration across benchmarks.

E.measurement.reason: Success uses the benchmarks own verification scripts with a 30-step cap and single-benchmark LLM judge not used for the main metric; deductions for corrected scripts / Windows adaptation (OSWorld-W) without validation and for baseline scores whose sources are not detailed.

E.causality.reason: Component on/off tables exist for each module and Operator-as-AppAgent isolates the HostAgent effect partially, but baselines get neither the 12 APIs nor the task-tailored docs, ablation baselines differ between tables (OSWorld-W 16.3 vs 22.4), step savings are computed on jointly-solved subsets, and gains are 1-3 tasks on a 49-task set.

E.holdout.reason: Help documents are written for the benchmark tasks, APIs are built for the benchmark Office apps, and the self-experience DB is filled from benchmark runs with no stated separation; no unseen applications; evaluation limited to two Windows benchmarks.

E.statistics.reason: Single runs; OSWorld-W increments of 2.04 points with headline gaps of 7 tasks; subset step comparisons on 10-34 tasks; internal inconsistency across tables; error analysis percentages without denominators.

E.cost.reason: Reports step counts, LLM and non-LLM latency per step (about 10 s per LLM call, +1 s hybrid detection), hardware (A100 for OmniParser, 8-core VMs) and a speculative-execution inference reduction; deductions for no token/dollar numbers, ACS on jointly solved subsets and no cost for authoring APIs/docs.
